policy: Named-species evidence permits source-scored admission with at least three supported core traits; held true UNKNOWN is legitimate, and variation is positive-only. No Hays wild specimen, county nativity, exact photo identity or plant status certification.

core_notes.head: Gould 1975 p.106: two-ranked unbranched ryegrass spike.
core_notes.habit: Texas A&M AgriLife exact species growth habit: bunch grass.
core_notes.ligule: Gould 1975 p.106: membranous inner leaf-collar ligule.
core_notes.awns: Gould 1975 p.106: lemmas can lack obvious awns or bear ONE up to 8 mm; conditional morphs, not simultaneous structures.

remaining_cautions: Mature ryegrass glumes and planting history are needed to separate perenne, multiflorum and hybrids.
admissions.field_rule: Look for the two-ranked spike, membranous ligule and basal bunch; awnless and occasionally short-awned lemmas are both documented.

core_notes.head: Gould 1975 p.173: two-ranked unbranched wheat spike.
core_notes.habit: Kew GrassBase, exact species: annual, caespitose.
core_notes.ligule: Diggs 1999 printed p.1334: membranous ligule; Gould prints disputed 1–3 cm versus independently 1–3 mm, so do not use length.
core_notes.awns: Gould 1975 p.173 and Diggs 1999 p.1334: cultivar-dependent awnless or long lemma awns; polymorphic OR.

remaining_cautions: Cultivated wheat is not automatically a wild Hays County occurrence.
Preserve Gould's contested ligule units as transcription, not a diagnostic measurement.
admissions.field_rule: Look for the wheat spike, basal tuft and auricles; cultivars may have long lemma awns or lack conspicuous awns.

core_notes.head: Gould 1975 p.378: narrow pinkish feathery panicle.
core_notes.habit: Texas A&M Plants of Texas Rangelands: perennial bunchgrass.
core_notes.ligule: Gould: a genuine ring of short ligular hairs, separate from upper collar hairs.
core_notes.awns: Gould: ELEVEN to FIFTEEN unequal TRUE terminal lemma awns ON ONE lemma, 2.5–5 mm longest.

remaining_cautions: A mature isolated lemma macro is still needed for the photo-identification teaching set.
admissions.field_rule: Look for the pinkish plume and 11–15 unequal awns from a SINGLE lemma; not Setaria bristles or bur spines.

core_notes.head: Gould 1975, exact Cenchrus ciliaris/Pennisetum ciliare: foxtail-like cylindrical head.
core_notes.habit: Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015 pp.58–59: cespitose crown, rhizomes present or absent.
core_notes.ligule: Gould: minute ciliate membrane; 1–1.5 mm is hair height, NOT membrane height.
core_notes.awns: Gould: 2–4 spikelets per cluster with soft 4–10 mm bristles basally joined in involucres, unlike separate Setaria bristles.

remaining_cautions: No photo-specific Hays voucher; all existing CC credits preserved.
Rhizomes are conditional, not required of every plant.
admissions.field_rule: Look for soft basally joined bristles around multiple spikelets; compare Setaria and hard sandburs with a hand lens.
